title: Microsoft Purview: archive SharePoint files with retention policies
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, administrator opt-in default, licensing and archive behaviour match the supplied notice and Microsoft documentation. The administrative paths stop short of their final controls, and the budget discussion should cite the billing documentation explicitly.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches New retention policy from Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration.
claims.fix: Extend the path for a static policy to 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations > Decide if you want to retain content, delete it, or both > Archive retained items in secure and compliant Microsoft 365 Archive to reduce cost'. The wizard route is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies and the final option at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-settings.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell or API operation configures this retention archive action.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention policy archive action Microsoft Graph API PowerShell. Read retention-settings and full New-/Set-RetentionComplianceRule references; search also returned New-/Set-ComplianceTag syntax. No archive-setting operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Archive > Connect a policy is the route into Archive billing connection.
claims.quote: Go to the Services tab and find Microsoft 365 Archive. Select Connect a policy, turn on the Connection status toggle for the billing policy, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and its rendered copy to 'Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Microsoft 365 Archive > Connect a policy > Connection status', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/archive/archive-setup.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Earlier tenants can use Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services for Archive enablement.
claims.quote: On the Pay-as-you-go services page, select the Settings tab. Under Storage services, select Archive. On the Microsoft 365 Archive panel, in the SharePoint site archive section, select the status toggle.
claims.fix: Replace the earlier-flow note with 'Earlier tenants may use Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Settings > Storage services > Archive > SharePoint site archive > status toggle instead', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/archive/archive-setup.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell operation connecting Archive to a pay-as-you-go billing policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Archive" billing connect policy "API" "PowerShell". Read archive-setup and pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node. Results described UI and unrelated Backup billing, not an Archive connection API.

claims.claim: No administrator UI is documented for hiding only the tenant's manual file Archive action while retaining policy archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: "AllowFileArchive" "admin center" disable manual UI; Microsoft 365 Archive AllowFileArchive disable manual archive admin center UI GCC High DoD OneDrive retention. Read archive-manage and archive-faq; manual-action controls are PowerShell, not UI.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: third table row and prose
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false hides manual file archiving across the tenant.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchive $false
This tenant setting overrides the site-level property with the same name and blocks manual file archiving across the tenant.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrators or Global Administrators can control manual file archiving.
claims.quote: SharePoint Administrators or Global Administrators can control manual file archiving for all SharePoint sites, a subset of sites, or not at all.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site_url> -AllowFileArchive $false hides manual Archive on a single site.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site_url> -AllowFileArchive $false
When set to False, users can't manually archive new files on the site, but existing archived files can still be reactivated.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault $false controls manual archiving on subsequently created sites.
claims.quote:
To control whether users can manually archive files on sites created in the future, use the -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault property of the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet.
Set-SPOTenant -AllowFileArchiveOnNewSitesByDefault $false

claims.claim: The New-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention archive action PowerShell New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-ComplianceTag archive parameter API. Read the full New-RetentionComplianceRule reference: no archive parameter; RetentionComplianceAction allows Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete.

claims.claim: The Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference lists no archive parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention archive action PowerShell New-RetentionComplianceRule Set-ComplianceTag archive parameter API. Read the full Set-RetentionComplianceRule reference: no archive parameter; RetentionComplianceAction allows Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete.

claims.claim: Adding the archive action in a policy or label's retention settings is necessary to make that retention configuration archive files.
claims.quote: Existing retention policies and labels don't archive files unless an administrator updates them to include the archive action.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining the E5 requirement and consumption-based Archive storage billing.
claims.quote: File-level archive requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license. No additional setup is required to archive files by using retention policies or labels. To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented consumption-based Archive storage meter.
claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate.

claims.claim: Archived files need reactivation before users can read them.
claims.quote: After a file is archived, it requires reactivation before it can be read.
